chapter_theme: Learning as the thing that makes a person see, belong anywhere, and possess what can't be lost. It begins and is only complete in conduct: to learn is also to stand by what is learned.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar's divisions: what to learn and why (391), the instruments of letters and numbers (392), the height of the learned against the unlearned (393-395), and the distinction of learning itself (396-400).

391.reading: Learn what is to be learned without flaw, and having learned, stand in keeping with it.
391.nuance: நிற்க gives conduct a posture: the chapter's first verse makes learning unfinished until one stands by it. Parimelazhagar narrows கற்பவை to works on the aims of life, on the grounds that life is too short for the rest, but the verse leaves the scope open.

392.reading: What are called numbers and what are called letters, these two, are called the eyes of living beings.
392.nuance: The verse says வாழும் உயிர்க்கு and doesn't restrict it. Parimelazhagar limits it to beings of special understanding and treats the two as tools for seeing the aims of life; Kalaignar goes further and makes them the test of being alive at all.

393.reading: Those called people with eyes are the learned; the unlearned have two sores on their face.
393.nuance: The insult works because the sore is in the same place and looks similar. Parimelazhagar adds that a merely physical eye gives pain through disease. Kalaignar draws an inference absent from the verse, that a blind person who is learned counts as having eyes.

394.reading: To meet with delight and part leaving others thinking of you: such is the way of the learned.
394.nuance: The measure of learning here is purely social, with no mention of knowledge. Manakkudavar makes it a comparison with two people who meet in joy and part in longing, an image close to love. Parimelazhagar's விளக்கம் opens the அத்தன்மைத்து to include right conduct and counsel.

395.reading: Those who learned while yearning like the poor before the rich are the foremost; those who did not learn are the lowest.

positions.position: The learner stands humbled before the teacher and is thereby foremost. Those ashamed of that posture stay low for good, having lost true learning to false pride.
positions.quote: செல்வர்முன் நல்கூர்ந்தார் நிற்குமாறு போலத் தாமும் ஆசிரியர்முன் ஏக்கற்று நின்றும் கற்றார் தலையாயினார்

positions.position: It is the unlearned who stand yearning like the poor, and they rank beneath the learned.

396.reading: A well in sand gives water as far as it is dug; for people, understanding wells up as far as they have learned.
396.nuance: ஊறும் matters: understanding seeps up from below rather than being poured in, so study opens something rather than simply filling a store. Parimelazhagar openly reconciles this with 373, saying it holds where fate doesn't oppose it.

positions.position: The verse holds where fate does not stand against it, and so it doesn't conflict with 373.

397.reading: Any land becomes one's own, any town one's own; why then does a person stay unlearned until death?
397.nuance: The verse states the belonging without naming who has it; the commentators supply the learned. Parimelazhagar's reason is reception: others' lands give the learned gifts and honour. A reader today may hear something more cosmopolitan than that.

398.reading: The learning one acquires in a single span serves as protection through seven.

positions.position: ஒருமை and எழுமை are births: learning stays with the soul as deeds do, and follows it into each birth.
positions.quote: வினைகள்போல உயிரின்கண் கிடந்து அது புக்குழிப் புகும்

positions.position: They are generations: what is learned in one generation protects seven generations of descendants.
positions.quote: ஒரு தலைமுறையில் பெறும் கல்வி அறிவனாது, ஏழேழு தலைமுறைக்கும் பாதுகாப்பாக அமையும்.

399.reading: Seeing that what delights them delights the world, the learned come to love it all the more.

positions.position: What they desire further is learning itself, because it delights the world too. Unlike wealth, its pleasure gains from being shared.
The learned are glad when others enjoy what they enjoy. The verse is about freedom from envy, a virtue that learning brings.
positions.quote: இஃது அழுக்காறு செய்யாது இன்புறுதல் அறமாதலின், அது கல்வியானே வருமென்றது.

400.reading: Learning is the imperishable, excellent wealth for a person; other things are not wealth.
400.nuance: மாடு is a plain word for property and cattle, and the verse flatly denies that other possessions deserve it. Parimelazhagar defines the imperishability as more than safety from thieves and kings: learning doesn't decrease when given away.

links.note: 391 demands standing by what is learned; 140 gives the failure's verdict: those who have learned much but can't act in accord with the world are unlearned and ignorant. Conduct can cancel the very category of learned.
Both turn eyes into sores, but by different tests: lack of learning here and lack of கண்ணோட்டம், kindly regard, in 575. One verse grounds sight in knowledge and the other in compassion.

In Parimelazhagar's reading, the two make one argument across chapters: learning travels with the soul through births, while caste rank ends with the body. That is why 409 can rank learning over birth.
396 makes understanding strictly proportional to study. In Parimelazhagar's reading of 416, even a small hearing gives full greatness. Reading gains by degree and listening at once.
